sentences.text: As per the facts of the case on 11.03.2014, at about 06.20 AM , the petitioner alongwith her family members were going in a car, from his house to Sadar Bazar Delhi.

And when they reached at main road Deenpur, opposite Dispensary New Delhi, suddenly a car bearing No. DL1LE8126 being driven by its driver came at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit their car from right side.
As a result of which petitioner and other occupants of the car received injuries . The petitioner was taken to R.T.R.M Hospital , New Delhi.
She has suffered simple injuries due to this accident.

2. The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving by (respondent no.3/ Driver) who was driving Vehicle No. DL 1LE8126.
The offending vehicle was owned by Sushil Bohra ( respondent no.1/owner) and was insured with M/S IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co Ltd (respondent no.2).

entities.text: IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co Ltd
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
The petitioner has filed the present claim thereby claiming a sum of Rs. 50,00,000/ ( Fifty Lacs ) from respondents as compensation,
alongwith interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.

3. The respondent No.1 has filed reply/WS stating therein that a MACT No. 132/16 Sharda vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 6 of 13 false case been filed against him to Sharda Devi vs Sushil Bohra on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86773435/
5 extort money from him.

sentences.text: It is stated that alleged accident pertains to some other incident in which petitioner might have been involved.

4. The respondent no. 2, Insurance company has filed its reply stating therein that insurance company is not liable to pay compensation amount as the offending vehicle was not insured with IFFCO Tokio General Insurance.
5. The respondent No.3 has not appeared in this case.

6. After completion of pleading, vide an order dated 16.07.2015, the following consolidated issues were framed in the present case as well in MACT No.614/14,
616/14,160/14 and 617/14.

(i) Whether Gun, Annu, Sharda Devi, Ashwani Chaurasia and Asha Ram Chaurasia sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt. 11.03.2014 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle No.
DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent No.3 ? OPP (ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation if so, what amount and from whom?
... OPP.

(iii) Relief.
7.
All the cases are consolidated for the purpose of evidence qua rash and negligence driving by R.3.
The petitioner examined herself as PW1.
Sh Aswhwani Chaurasia as PW2.
Ms Anuu as PW3.
The respondent No.1 examined himself as RW1/A.
The respondent No.2 has examined Sh Rajat Saini as R2W1.
R.3 has not examined any witness.
8. I have heard ld. counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld Counsel MACT No. 132/16 Sharda vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 7 of 13 for the respondent No.2.
None appeared on behalf of R.1 and R.3 to argue the case.

My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No. (i): Whether Gun, Annu,
Sharda Devi, Ashwani Chaurasia and Asha Ram Chaurasia sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt. 11.03.2014 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle No. DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent No.3 ?
OPP 9.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.
Petitioner, herself examined as PW1.
Sh Ashwani Chaurasia as PW2 and Ms Anuu as PW3 10.

PW 1 in her evidence, filed by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, has deposed that on 11.03.2014, at about 06.20 AM , she alongwith her family members were going in a car from her house to Sadar Bazar Delhi.

She has deposed that when they reached at main road, Deenpur opposite Dispensary New Delhi, suddenly a car bearing No. DL1LE8126 being driven by its driver came at a very high speed and in rash and negligent manner hit their car from right side.
As a result of which petitioner and other occupants of car received injuries .
The petitioner was taken to R.T.R.M Hospital , New Delhi.
She has suffered injuries due to this accident.

PW2 and PW3 have deposed on the same lines Sharda Devi vs Sushil Bohra on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86773435/
6 as deposed by PW.1 11.PW 1 , PW2 and PW3 have been crossexamined, but nothing material could come out in their cross examination which could disbelief their testimony.

The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict MACT No. 132/16 Sharda vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 8 of 13 as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.

sentences.text: It is a matter of record that there is no evidence at all to show that victim's car driver was at fault, in any way.
12.The fact that petitioner suffered injuries in that accident is also supported by the medical documents Mark A.
After investigation, police has also indicted respondent no. 1 as an accused for the offences punishable under Sections 279/337/338 IPC.
The case has been registered against respondent no. 3.
The fact of accident and the respondent no.3 is facing the trial as an accused is not disputed.

Considering all these facts, it stands proved that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a car bearing No.DL1LE8126 by respondent no. 3 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
ISSUE No.2: ? Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom?
Being injured, petitioner is well within her rights to claim compensation.
It is there on record, as per the deposition of PW 1 and the discharged card Ex Mark A.
The petitioner was removed to RTRM Hospital for her treatment.
It is deposed by her that due to the said accident, she herself and her family members have suffered great mental pain, agony, love and affection, loss of social activities etc.

14. So considering all the facts compensation is awarded as under:
MEDICAL EXPENSES 15.
The petitioner has not placed on record medical bills of Rs.1205/ MACT No. 132/16 Sharda vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 9 of 13

entities.text: Rs.1205/ MACT No. 132/16 Sharda vs Sushil Bohra & ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no rebuttal to these medical bills Ex PW1/1 ( Colly).
But , seeing the age of injured and nature of injuries being suffered by petitioner, a lump sum amount of Rs.5,000/ is granted to her towards medical expenses. .
Attendant Charges , Conveyance and Special Diet.
16. As far as attendant charges are concerned petitioner has not led any PE in this regard

, yet,
considering the stay of hospitalization of petitioner seeing the nature of injuries being suffered by petitioner , an amount of Rs.2,000/, is being awarded for attendant charges.
Moreover, a sum of Rs. 2,000/ for special diets, Rs.2,000/ for conveyance is also awarded to the petitioner.
Pain and suffering 17.

The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which she got medical treatment and she was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
After the accident, petitioner was taken to RTRM Hospital New Delhi.

It is very much apparent that when a Sharda Devi vs Sushil Bohra on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86773435/
7 person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which she faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
To compensate petitioner under this head, a sum of Rs.15,000/ is awarded to her.
MACT No. 132/16 Sharda vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 10 of 13 Mental and physical shock:

18 . The petitioner was 60 years of age at the time of accident but due to this mishappening with her, all her dreams and expectations got completely shattered which cannot be compensated in monetary terms.
However, to console him to an extent, a sum of Rs.10,000/ is awarded to petitioner under this head.

19. Thus making a total of Rs.36,000/ detail of which is given as under:
(i) Medical expenses Rs. 5,000/
(ii) Attendant charges Rs. 2,000/
(ii) Special diets Rs. 2,000/
(iii) Conveyance Rs. 2,000/
(v) Pain & suffering Rs. 15,000/
(vi) Mental & physical shock Rs. 10,000/ Total Rs. 36,000/
20.

This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondent by holding that accident in question took place due to rash or negligent driving of Car bearing No.DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent no.3 and petitioner suffered injuries in that accident and petitioner is entitled for compensation.
21. Now the question arises who will pay the compensation amount.
The only submission of Ld Counsel for insurance company is that the Insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
It is submitted that offending vehicle is not insured with IFFCO Tokio General Insurance company Ltd at the time of accident.

(i) Whether Gun, Annu, Sharda Devi, Ashwani Chaurasia and Asha Ram Chaurasia sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt. 11.03.2014 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle No.
DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent No.3 ? OPP (ii) Whether the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation if so, what amount and from whom?
My issuewise findings are as under: ISSUE No. (i): Whether Gun, Annu,
Sharda Devi, Ashwani Chaurasia and Asha Ram Chaurasia sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt. 11.03.2014 due to rash or negligent driving of vehicle No. DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent No.3 ?
ISSUE No.2: ? Whether the petitioner in the above mentioned case is entitled to claim compensation , if so , what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.facts:
And when they reached at main road Deenpur, opposite Dispensary New Delhi, suddenly a car bearing No. DL1LE8126 being driven by its driver came at a very high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit their car from right side.
As a result of which petitioner and other occupants of the car received injuries . The petitioner was taken to R.T.R.M Hospital , New Delhi.
She has suffered simple injuries due to this accident.
2. The present application/claim petition has been filed contending that said accident took place, due to rash and negligent driving by (respondent no.3/ Driver) who was driving Vehicle No. DL 1LE8126.
The offending vehicle was owned by Sushil Bohra ( respondent no.1/owner) and was insured with M/S IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Co Ltd (respondent no.2).
The petitioner has filed the present claim thereby claiming a sum of Rs. 50,00,000/ ( Fifty Lacs ) from respondents as compensation,
alongwith interest @ 18% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The proof of negligence while disposing of a claim application under MACT, is not that strict MACT No. 132/16 Sharda vs Sushil Bohra & ors Page No. 8 of 13 as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The case has been registered against respondent no. 3.
, yet,
considering the stay of hospitalization of petitioner seeing the nature of injuries being suffered by petitioner , an amount of Rs.2,000/, is being awarded for attendant charges.
The next point that is to be discussed is pain and suffering and to calculate the same, the nature of injuries caused to the injured due to the accident, duration for which she got medical treatment and she was constrained to live in bed are few factors which must be taken into account.
After the accident, petitioner was taken to RTRM Hospital New Delhi.
It is very much apparent that when a Sharda Devi vs Sushil Bohra on 13 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/86773435/
7 person is leading a normal life suddenly meets with an accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which she faces cannot be considered.
The whole life changes and everything looks darker to that person which can be beyond out of imagination, such a scenario could shake even braver of bravest.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
This issue is therefore decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondent by holding that accident in question took place due to rash or negligent driving of Car bearing No.DL1LE8126 being driven by respondent no.3 and petitioner suffered injuries in that accident and petitioner is entitled for compensation.
IFFCO Tokio General Insurance Company Ltd.
Reliance is placed on ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Ltd Vs Ashokan &
Ors C.M.A No. 275 of 2016 and CMP No.2312 of 2016 of Hon'ble Madras High Court and Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd Vs Arvind Dattatray Shindode, First Appeal N0. 55 of 2023 of Hon'ble Bombay High Court.
